Chapter 16 of 18

The Nocturnals

After HoursTrout Lake → industrial East Van150 BPM
The story

After dark, the coyotes leave Trout Lake. They slip through alleys, rail cuts, empty lots and service roads toward warehouse rooms that do not advertise themselves. Raccoons come along. Crows who are off shift come along. These are the Nocturnals, and they always know where the music is before any human does.

They are curious, indulgent and badly supervised. They attend the Morning Meeting, though nobody is sure how much attention they pay. They pass through the Green Static without losing their way, and they lead people toward the Sixth Hour with a look that says: this way, obviously. Some wander off toward the Endless Stair and take a while to come back.

The city trusts them exactly as much as it should, which is not very much. Never trust an animal that already knows the address. Night eyes. Follow bass. No address. They know.

17 · Deep Night beginsThe Eternal Night

The deepest nocturnal phase. Stores the darkness, time and visual noise the city cannot use during daylight, and keeps culture, machinery, animals and hidden systems running after ordinary city life has receded.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
